findings.what: `body_rows - 1` underflows when the pane body has zero rows (tiny terminal), panicking in debug and wrapping to usize::MAX in release so the page covers the whole feed, whereas the removed loop handled body_rows == 0 and returned 1.

The removed loop filled the full `body_rows` budget (stopping only when `used + row > body_rows`), but the replacement fits the window into `body_rows - 1`, so unless tail_window_start's fit rule is deliberately off by one, a backward page is now one row shorter than the forward page derived from `shown.len()`, reintroducing the up/down page-size mismatch the doc comment says was fixed.
